## COPG v7.7.2

*Protected apps that used to close on launch with COPG installed now work, plus a new device field and more complete translations.*

### Protected apps — fixed
*   **Some apps closed instantly when COPG was installed, even with no spoof set on them.** A few apps wrapped in certain third-party protectors would detect COPG and exit on launch (untagged apps included). COPG now leaves no trace in those apps unless you actually turn a spoof on, so they launch and stay open normally.
*   **Extra stealth hardening** for apps that unload COPG after spoofing, so nothing of COPG is left behind for an app to find.

### Device profile
*   **Separate Device field.** `Build.DEVICE` (the product device codename) is now its own field in the device modal. Leave it blank to keep matching the fingerprint automatically; fill it only if you need a different value.

### Translations
*   **Arabic, German, Spanish, Indonesian, Thai and Chinese are now complete** — every screen is fully translated.

## COPG v7.7.1

*Works on Zygisk Next 1.5.3 again, your config survives updates, and a few device-profile and WebUI additions.*

### Zygisk Next 1.5.3 — fixed
*   **COPG spoofed nothing on Zygisk Next 1.5.3.** The new Zygisk Next stopped granting a permission COPG used to read its own config, so every app looked "not configured" and ran unspoofed (the license still showed valid). COPG now ships that permission itself, so it works on 1.5.3 and older versions alike.

### Updates keep your setup
*   **Updating no longer wipes your config.** Every update used to replace your devices, packages and tags with the defaults. Now your existing COPG.json and list.json are kept, and the install screen says so. A missing or broken file still falls back to the default.

### Device profile
*   **Custom system props editor.** In a device's advanced section you can now fake any short existing system prop (for example `ril.product_code`, `ril.official_cscver`, `ro.omc.build.version`) for apps with COW Prop Spoof (`cow`) on.
*   **Base OS field.** New build field for `Build.VERSION.BASE_OS` (and the matching prop for `cow` apps).
*   **Separate Product field.** Product was silently overwritten with the model on every save, so a real product name (e.g. `e3qxxx` vs model `SM-S928B`) could never be set. It's its own field now; left blank it falls back to the fingerprint's product, then the model.

### WebUI
*   **Edit several packages together.** Long-press to select packages, then **Edit together**: change only the toggles you want (device, GPU, `cow`, `aid`, …) and they apply to every selected app, leaving each app's other settings as they were. Handy for clones and per-user copies.

releases.body:
## COPG v7.7.0

*Three new per-app spoofs — Wi-Fi MAC, Bluetooth MAC and boot id — plus SKU build fields, and the GPU spoof unlocks a game's high-graphics options again.*

### Wi-Fi MAC — new
*   **Fake the Wi-Fi MAC per app (`mac`).** An app now reads a MAC you control instead of the phone's real one: `mac` for a steady fake, `mac=rnd` for a fresh one each launch, or `mac=<12 hex>` to set an exact address. **PRO.** Resident and behind the use-at-your-own-risk gate — never for competitive games.

### Bluetooth MAC — new
*   **Fake the Bluetooth MAC per app (`btmac`).** The same three forms — `btmac`, `btmac=rnd`, `btmac=<12 hex>` — for the Bluetooth address a device check can read. **PRO**, stealth (nothing stays mapped after it applies).

### Boot ID — new
*   **Per-app boot id (`bootid`).** Each app gets its own boot id, so a value that's meant to be the same for every app since the last reboot no longer links your accounts together. **PRO**, behind the use-at-your-own-risk gate.

### SKU — new
*   **SKU and ODM SKU added to the device profile.** Two more build fields you can set per device, so an app that reads the device SKU (for example the SKU row in DevCheck) sees the spoofed phone instead of your real one.

### GPU spoof — unlocks high graphics again
*   **Games that gate max FPS / HD on a flagship GPU unlock it on the spoofed profile.** The GPU spoof now reaches the exact GPU read those games use to decide which graphics options to offer, so the high-end presets open up again. *(Still resident/detectable and behind the use-at-your-own-risk gate — never for competitive games.)*
*   **Monster Hunter Outlanders added to the device list**, ready-made with a flagship GPU so its high-graphics options unlock out of the box (both the Global and TW/HK/MO builds). **Needs PRO** — it uses the GPU spoof.

### Other fixes
*   **Hide dev-options / USB-debugging — stronger.** Now also hides it from apps that read the setting straight from the system instead of the normal lookup (a path a few detectors like Momo use), so the app still sees it off.
*   **System-server spoofs — lower battery & CPU use.** They now wake only when you actually change a setting, instead of re-reading the config a few times a second around the clock — so they use noticeably less CPU and battery while idle, and a toggle still applies instantly.
*   **GPU Vulkan stability** — fixed a crash at launch on some devices when the GPU spoof was on.
*   **Resident hooks leave a cleaner footprint** — the inline hooks no longer leave a writable-and-executable page mapped, a pattern some scanners flag as tampering. More hardening here is still in progress.
*   **Locale spoof** — no longer affects system processes (issue #80).
*   **Root detection** — the System tab reads the *active* root manager, not a leftover binary from one you switched away from.
*   **WebUI** — a brand filter on the Devices tab; forms no longer overflow the screen in landscape.
*   **Translations** — all 8 community languages brought fully up to date (Arabic, German, Spanish, Indonesian, Portuguese-BR, Thai, Turkish, Chinese), including every string added or reworded since the last sync.

### Heads up
*   **32-bit phones are no longer supported** — this release is 64-bit (arm64) only. Nearly every phone from the last several years is 64-bit, so this affects only very old devices.

## COPG v7.6.1

*Makes the per-app ANDROID_ID spoof consistent across every read path, and fixes a `getprop` that could leak the real value.*

### ANDROID_ID — consistent everywhere
*   **The `aid` spoof no longer disagrees with itself.** Before, an app could read the faked ANDROID_ID from the normal settings lookup but still get the *real* one through a direct provider `query`/`call`, or by reading `settings_ssaid.xml` — and that mismatch is itself a giveaway. The `aid` tag now spoofs the value in the system server at the source, so every read path returns the same ID. The **Hook Status** screen gained an ANDROID_ID consistency badge on the `aid` row so you can confirm it at a glance.

### getprop — matches the API
*   **A shelled-out `getprop` now returns the spoofed value.** Closed a case where a `getprop` run through a wrapped shell slipped past the spoof and exposed the real property, so the command line and the framework API agree again.

### Other
*   Stability and hardening fixes.

releases.body:
## COPG v7.6.0

*Android 17 support, a new one-tap Random Device identity, an Integrations dashboard, a stealthier CPU-spoof backend, and a batch of crash and compatibility fixes.*

### Android 17 — supported
*   **COPG now runs on Android 17 (SDK 37).** Earlier builds could boot-loop a phone on A17 as soon as a system-wide hook (CorePatch, Google Account, Wallpaper ID, locale, VPN-hide, and friends) tried to install. The v7878 engine is now built from source and made A17-safe, so those device-wide hooks arm cleanly on the new release. If you were stuck on A16 or had the system-server spoofs gated off, they're back on.
    *   *Engine A17 fix: big thanks to the **HMA OSS** developer for the engine fix that made this possible.*

### Random Device — new
*   **A one-tap random phone.** The device list has a new **Random** profile at the top: pick it and the app sees a complete, self-consistent made-up phone — brand, model, fingerprint and build fields that all match — instead of a specific preset. It sits alongside **This Device** as a pinned option in the device picker. **FREE.**
*   **Fresh identity every launch (`randid`).** With the new **Randomize IDs** switch on a package, every derived identifier that COPG can roll — ANDROID_ID, serial, GAID, App Set ID, IMEI, wallpaper ID — is re-rolled each time the app launches, so it looks like a brand-new device on every start rather than one stable fake. Pair it with the Random profile for a full rotation, or use it on any profile. **PRO**, stealth where the underlying spoof is stealth.

### Integrations dashboard — new
*   **See the tools COPG is working with.** A new **Integrations** sheet under Settings lists the root manager, the Zygisk implementation and optional helper modules (such as NoMount) that COPG detects, each with a live status — active, installed, or absent — and its version. If a helper is too old to use safely (an out-of-date NoMount), it's flagged **Update needed** with a tap-to-read explanation of what to do. Makes it obvious at a glance what's powering the module on your setup.

### CPU spoof — stealthier backend
*   **Hides the CPU swap from mount scanners (optional).** When the **NoMount** kernel module is installed, the per-app `/proc/cpuinfo` spoof now goes through NoMount's in-kernel path redirect instead of a bind mount — so it no longer shows up in the app's own `/proc/self/mountinfo` (the trace that some anti-cheats flag as tampering). Without NoMount, COPG falls back to the normal bind mount, unchanged. The on-boot foreground reconcile honors the NoMount backend too.
*   **Needs NoMount 2.2.0 or newer.** Older NoMount builds had a kernel freeze/panic bug, so COPG now uses the traceless redirect only on 2.2.0+ and automatically stays on the safe bind mount on anything older (the Integrations card flags a NoMount that's too old).

### Zygisk status — improved
*   **Correct Zygisk name and version in the System tab.** The System tab now reports the real Zygisk implementation (Zygisk Next, ReZygisk, BReZygisk), its version, and whether it's actually injecting vs merely installed — read straight from the daemon rather than guessed, so a misnamed or disabled variant is no longer reported wrong.

### GPU spoof — fixed
*   **No more crash on Android 16 / newer chips.** On ARMv8.5 devices (and newer ROMs that map system libraries with branch-target hardening), turning on the GPU spoof could crash an app at launch with a `SIGILL` — most visibly games that query Vulkan during start-up. The inline hook now keeps the required landing instruction at the patch site, so it's safe on every device. *(The GPU spoof stays resident/detectable and behind the use-at-your-own-risk gate — still never for competitive games.)*

### Concurrent Mic — fixed
*   **Turning it off no longer needs a reboot.** Disabling **Concurrent Mic** now takes effect live; previously the audio server couldn't read the toggle under SELinux, so the feature stayed on until the next reboot.

### CorePatch — fixed
*   **No more Samsung lock/reboot loop.** On some Samsung devices the signature-verification patch could trip a "device locked, try again in 3 days" / inactivity-reboot loop. The signature check is now scoped to the package installer only (not every signature comparison on the device), and the mis-triggered Samsung inactivity-reboot is handled, so the loop is gone.

### Other fixes
*   **SIM/carrier** — a shelled-out `getprop` of the carrier props now matches what the API reports (closes a `getprop`-vs-API mismatch for `sim`/`simx`).
*   **VPN hide** — reports the real underlying interface so a VPN-detector no longer sees a network-type mismatch; added an older-Android file-view layer for `vpnn`.
*   **Home** — tap the **Devices** / **Packages** stat cards to jump straight to that Library tab.

### Thanks
*   **Huge thanks to @PARADOXCODM** for testing roughly **20 Android 17 builds** back-to-back while we chased the boot loop — including having to **factory-reset his own device** after one of our builds bricked the boot. A17 support in this release exists because of that patience. 🙏
*   Thanks to the **HMA OSS** developer for the v7878 engine fix behind the Android 17 support.

*Hotfix: Concurrent Mic now works on the official release build.*

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

The white flash on opening the WebUI. It was two things stacked.

The `html` element had no background colour, only `body` did. Until `body` renders, the WebView paints the root element, which defaults to white. That is the flash you see. `html` now uses the same dark colour as `body`, and `color-scheme: dark` is set so form controls and scrollbars follow.

`theme-color` is set too, which the WebView uses for its own loading surface.

The language redirect was worse. It lived in the script at the end of `body`, so if you had picked English before, opening the WebUI would fully load the Chinese page first, then jump to the English one. Two loads, two flashes. It is in `head` now and uses `location.replace`, so only one page loads and no extra history entry is created.

Also the first `load()` call now runs in `setTimeout(..., 0)`, so the browser paints the interface before doing any of the shell round-trips.

Expect it to still take a moment to open. That is the manager creating the WebView and injecting the bridge, which the module cannot shorten. What is gone is the white part.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

The log showed the profile being applied three times on every boot:

```
13:45:23 已应用预设: balanced
13:45:23 initrc 服务已应用预设 balanced
13:45:24 已应用预设: balanced
13:45:36 已应用预设: balanced
```

`initrc` applies once, `service.sh` applies again, and `appwatch` applies a third time on its first poll because it started with an empty `last` and saw a change.

Each apply walks a few dozen nodes. Three of them back to back is a noticeable chunk of the startup lag, and the third one lands half a minute after boot, which is exactly when things feel worst.

Changes:
- a marker keyed by `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, so only the first caller applies and the rest skip. Whatever starts first wins; order does not matter.
- `appwatch` seeds `last` with the current base profile instead of an empty string, so startup no longer triggers a redundant apply.
- `post-fs-data` removes the previous boot's marker.

Verified: same boot id applies once then skips, a new boot id applies again.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

This is the actual cause of the lag. The IO scheduler I changed last release was a real problem, but not the main one.

`initrc` starts `KernelSU-Tuner_watch` with `appwatch.sh run` directly, which skips the switch check that lives in the `start` branch. So with `APPWATCH=0` the foreground polling kept running anyway. You can see it in the log you sent:

```
13:45:31 启动
13:45:36 默认 -> balanced
13:51:11 默认 -> performance
```

That is the appwatch loop, while the switch was off.

What it does every 3 seconds is `dumpsys activity activities`. That is one of the heaviest commands in Android and it holds the ActivityManager lock while it builds its output. The back gesture, launching WeChat, opening the WebUI all need that same lock, so everything waits a beat and then continues, over and over.

Fixes:
- `run_loop` checks the switch itself now and exits immediately when it is off, so it cannot be started around the check any more.
- the poll interval went from 3 seconds to 10.
- `fg_pkg` tries `dumpsys window` first, which is far smaller. It only falls back to `dumpsys activity activities` if that returns nothing.

After installing, reboot. The old polling process belongs to the previous version and only goes away on restart.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

The IO scheduler was the main cause. Samsung ships `ssg` as the default scheduler on this device, and the module replaced it with `none`. Every block IO goes through that scheduler, so changing it makes everything feel one beat slower: back gesture, opening a chat, even loading the WebUI.

The scheduler is only replaced now if the current one is `cfq` or `deadline`, both old and long past their best. Vendor schedulers (`ssg`, `none`, `mq-deadline`, `bfq`, `kyber`) are left alone.

Each apply also restores the recorded original first, then decides whether to change anything. That means simply installing this and applying once puts `ssg` back for you; no manual revert needed.

Also in this build:
- `read_ahead_kb` dropped a lot: 128 power save, 256 balanced, 512 performance, 1024 gaming. It used to write 2048 on performance, against a stock value of 128. Over-reading hurts random IO more than it helps.
- performance and gaming keep `walt` if the kernel has it, instead of forcing `performance`. Samsung defaults to `walt`; forcing `performance` just builds heat and gets throttled later.
- turning a switch off now actually restores the node. `CPU_GOV`, `CPU_FREQ`, `IO_SCHED` and `READ_AHEAD` restore their recorded originals when disabled. Before, disabling only stopped future writes, so anything already changed stayed changed, which is why flipping switches did nothing.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

Two things were making the S25 Ultra slow.

First, the balanced profile replaced the CPU governor. Samsung ships `performance` as the governor, and the balanced candidate list started with `schedutil`, so applying the balanced profile quietly downgraded the whole device. Balanced no longer touches the governor at all. Powersave still switches it, and performance/gaming still set `performance`.

Second, the IO tuning walked every entry under `/sys/block`. On this device that is 160 `loop` devices plus a couple of dozen `dm-*` mappings, so every apply wrote close to four hundred nodes. It now skips `loop`, `dm`, `ram`, `zram` and `sr`, and only touches real storage.

Verified against a mock of the S25 Ultra layout: after applying balanced, both clusters keep `performance` and their original frequency range.

If you already have it installed, either uninstall and reinstall cleanly, or run `tuner.sh revert` first so the old governor value goes back.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

Three switches were writing to the system even when turned off.

The thermal unlock switch, while off, forced every `thermal_zone` to `enabled`. That means each apply re-armed all the throttling limits even though you never asked for the unlock. It leaves them alone now.

Same pattern for the IPv6 switch: while off, it set `disable_ipv6=0` on every interface. On a network where IPv6 does not actually work, the system tries it first and waits for the timeout before falling back, which makes things slower. It does nothing now, and the uninstall script behaves the same way.

The DNS preset pointed the system private DNS at `dns.google` on the performance profile. That does not resolve in China. It uses `opportunistic` now: encrypted when the network offers it, otherwise the carrier DNS, and it cannot break connectivity. Balanced and powersave stop touching that setting entirely; before they would turn off a private DNS you configured yourself.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

This fixes the slowdown reported on the Galaxy S25 Ultra, and it was my bug.

The frequency floor and ceiling were taken from the first and last entry of the kernel's frequency table. That assumes the table is sorted ascending. On kernels that list frequencies from high to low, max and min came out reversed, and every core ended up pinned to the lowest step. Reading the list is now order-independent: the real minimum and maximum are compared directly.

Running the same code against a descending table now gives min 800 MHz / max 1.8 GHz instead of 300 MHz for both.

Also in this build:
- `walt` and `sugov_ext` added to the governor candidates. Qualcomm and Samsung kernels expose those, so the CPU governor switch was silently doing nothing there.
- `watermark_scale_factor` lowered from 150 to 100. 150 makes the kernel start reclaiming with plenty of memory still free.
- boot TRIM is off by default now. On large flash fstrim saturates IO for a minute or two after boot.
- balanced no longer caps the GPU performance level at half.
- removed three functions that were defined twice in `tuner.sh`, plus a duplicated frequency block.

If you are on 3.5.3 or older and your device feels slow, uninstall and reboot, then install this. Do not overwrite while the old config is still applying.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

Security work this release.

Custom parameters could write to a handful of nodes that either kill the device or run arbitrary code: `/proc/sysrq-trigger`, `/proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern`, `/proc/sys/kernel/modprobe`, `/proc/sys/kernel/hotplug`, `/sys/kernel/uevent_helper`, and the raw memory devices. Those are refused now.

The wipe guard missed several ways to erase a device: `blkdiscard`, `sgdisk --zap`, `mke2fs`, `fdisk`, `parted`, and `dd` aimed at `/dev/mmcblk` or `/dev/nvme`. A path containing `..` could also slip past the allowlist. All covered now.

Backup import copied config values straight in, newlines included, so a crafted file could append extra keys to `config.conf`. Newlines are flattened to spaces now.

`appwatch.sh set` did not validate its arguments, so a package name containing `|` corrupted the rules file. It checks both the package name and the preset name now.

Two places in the WebUI read a value back out of a DOM attribute and pasted it into a shell command without quoting. Both are escaped now.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

Config writes are atomic now. Four scripts still used `sed -i` followed by an append, which leaves a half-written `config.conf` if the write is interrupted. They all go through a temp file and a rename now.

User input reaching the shell is escaped. The custom parameter, backup import, preset name and per-app fields used to be wrapped in bare single quotes, so a value containing a quote broke the command. Input is escaped properly now.

`tuner.sh` and `cfg.sh` shared the same lock directory, so running both could stall one for up to 150 seconds. `cfg.sh` uses its own lock now.

releases.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

Four of the daemons could not actually be turned off. `autopilot`, `guard`, `appwatch` and `wipeshield` all started unconditionally when asked, and the watchdog asks every five minutes. So turning one off in the WebUI lasted until the next watchdog pass. Each one now checks its own switch first and refuses to start when it is disabled.

The watchdog also looked for `wipeshield.pid` while the script writes `shield.pid`, so it never saw the wipe guard as running. That is mapped now.

The language button stored your choice but nothing ever read it back. Both interfaces now check it on load, so picking English actually sticks.

The released zip was missing `module.yaml`, the icons, both READMEs, the license and the changelog. That was true of every release since 3.1.0. It now contains the full tree, which also means the GPL text ships with the binary.

stable.body:
Install through the KernelSU manager under Modules - Install from storage, then reboot.

The white flash on opening the WebUI. It was two things stacked.

The `html` element had no background colour, only `body` did. Until `body` renders, the WebView paints the root element, which defaults to white. That is the flash you see. `html` now uses the same dark colour as `body`, and `color-scheme: dark` is set so form controls and scrollbars follow.

`theme-color` is set too, which the WebView uses for its own loading surface.

The language redirect was worse. It lived in the script at the end of `body`, so if you had picked English before, opening the WebUI would fully load the Chinese page first, then jump to the English one. Two loads, two flashes. It is in `head` now and uses `location.replace`, so only one page loads and no extra history entry is created.

Also the first `load()` call now runs in `setTimeout(..., 0)`, so the browser paints the interface before doing any of the shell round-trips.

Expect it to still take a moment to open. That is the manager creating the WebView and injecting the bridge, which the module cannot shorten. What is gone is the white part.

# MagicNet v1.8.5

本次发行候选为 `v1.8.5` / `10613`，默认模板增加五个指定目标的拦截规则，以及 16 个大陆教育服务域名后缀的默认直连分流。

## 指定目标拦截

| 精确域名 | 目标端口 |
| --- | --- |
| `flash.sec.miui.com` | 不限 |
| `fraud-detection.engine.miui.com` | 不限 |
| `eps.caict.ac.cn` | 不限 |
| `gateway-papa.cloud.weizhi.com` | 不限 |
| `dm.wo.com.cn` | 仅 `18080`，TCP/UDP |

两个原生 `action: reject` 规则位于既有 DNS、嗅探、ICMP 和 `0.0.0.0` 处理之后、模式与应用及业务分流之前。命中目标的应用流量在 `rule`、`global`、`direct` 模式下均先执行拒绝；域名按完整名称匹配，父域名和子域名沿用原有规则。`dm.wo.com.cn` 的其他端口也沿用原有规则。

这些拒绝规则保留既有 DNS 捕获和解析处理，作用于进入 sing-box 且能识别目标域名的流量；使用纯 IP 且缺少域名信息的连接继续按原有规则处理。

## 大陆教育网站默认直连

以下后缀匹配根域名及其子域名，复用现有 `cn-direct` 组，默认选择 `direct`。用户对该组的选择继续保留。

| 范围 | 域名后缀 |
| --- | --- |
| 学校与教育科研域名 | `edu.cn` |
| 教育公共服务 | `moe.gov.cn`、`chsi.com.cn`、`smartedu.cn`、`neea.cn`、`ncss.cn` |
| 慕课与教学平台 | `icourse163.org`、`icourses.cn`、`xuetangx.com`、`yuketang.cn`、`chaoxing.com`、`zhihuishu.com` |
| 教育资讯与学术资源 | `eol.cn`、`cnki.net`、`wanfangdata.com.cn`、`cqvip.com` |

教育规则位于既有模式、LAN、用户与应用分流、广告和 DNS 防护之后，优先于后续国外学术、AI、游戏、开发及媒体分类。DNS 使用相同的 16 个后缀和现有本地加密解析器；前置 DNS 规则继续优先。

范围以此清单为准，其他教育网站与共享 CDN 沿用原有规则。各域名的官方来源见[策略库存](https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/MagicNet/blob/main/recipes/magicnet-routing-policy/POLICY_INVENTORY.md)。

## 安装与更新

规则随本版内置模板分发。正式发行后，新安装和正常升级使用该模板，无需额外执行社区模板更新；更新后按模块管理器提示重启。

## 验证要求与范围

模板层需验证精确拦截、教育后缀与边界负例、规则优先级及 DNS 对应；生成配置须通过锁定内核校验。正式发行还需通过固定源码的官方模块构建、完整质量与 Android/KernelSU 模拟器门槛。实际结果与来源提交记录于主仓库的 `recipes/magicnet/VERIFICATION.md`；发行时由附件 `build-source.json` 记录构建来源。

当前尚未公开发行，未进行真机安装或真实应用流量验收。

# MagicNet v1.8.4

修复 [#434](https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/MagicNet/issues/434)：未设置订阅 User-Agent 时，curl 默认标识可能被订阅服务或 CDN 以 HTTP 403 拒绝。现在默认标识遇到 403 时，同一次更新内改用 `clash.meta` 重试一次；该值不会写入配置，也不会覆盖用户自定义的 User-Agent。仍被拒绝时，日志提示在订阅设置中选择客户端 User-Agent。

订阅地址解析把 IPv4-mapped IPv6（`::ffff:a.b.c.d`）按嵌入的 IPv4 校验和钉选，避免 Rust 与 shell 双重校验不一致导致公网地址被误拒。

MCP 通用 `magicnet_file_read` 不再读取路由/屏蔽域名清单、`block.conf` 和 `proxy-chain.json`；通用 `magicnet_cli` 拒绝人类 `warp`/`node`/`route`/`block` 默认清单。具名的 `magicnet_node_list`、`magicnet_node_current`、`magicnet_block_list` 仍可显式使用。删除无调用方的 `magicnet_prepare_singbox_nodes` 包装。

本地验证：源码 Rust fmt/clippy/全部测试与 106 项 shell 主机回归通过（含真实 curl+HTTPS 的 403 回退用例）；配方检查与发布脚本测试通过。未进行真机安装验收；#434 的修复基于用户日志中的 HTTP 403，尚需报告者在设备上确认。

releases.body:
# MagicNet v1.8.2

本补丁版维护现有 Android root / arm64 实现，整合订阅更新、MCP 隐私边界与手机端可用性修复。

- 为最多五个来源的订阅更新设置独立、有界的批处理预算，避免沿用普通命令 180 秒期限而过早终止；各来源获取、转换及退出后的回滚仍有限时，控制进程退出后的清理预算不随批处理放大。
- WebUI 正确追踪私密订阅应用任务，保留进行中与失败反馈；增加跨来源同名 WebSocket 节点与退出恢复回归。
- MCP 通用文件接口拒绝热点恢复记录、应用 UID/包名清单、selector 选择和接口名等私密文件，包括 staging/backup 名称；通用 CLI 拒绝人类热点和应用清单输出。继续使用具名工具及脱敏 JSON 状态，不削弱 canonical 状态接口。
- 改善窄屏导航、编辑器、终端和应用列表使用体验，并避免空终端按钮被手机底栏遮挡。
- 同步固定的 sing-box 1.15.0-alpha.13 内核与配置来源，保留 tun/ebpf、事务回滚和最小披露合同。

## 安装与更新

`magicnet_installer.zip`、`MagicNet.zip` 和 `MagicNet-core.zip` 是字节一致的核心包兼容下载名。`MagicNet-full.zip` 包含离线组件；组件 ZIP 不能单独作为模块安装。更新后按管理器提示重启，保留用户配置与订阅。

默认仍为 `tun` / `magicnet0`，只允许显式 `tun|ebpf`；eBPF 依赖设备内核的 cgroup/TC 能力。`SHA256SUMS` 用于完整性校验，不是独立公钥签名。

## 验证范围与限制

源码本地执行 Rust、shell、组件、WebUI 类型/单元/构建与浏览器回归；正式发行须另通过固定提交的官方模块构建、完整质量与 Android/KernelSU 模拟器门槛。发布状态与最终来源 SHA 见主仓库的配方验证记录及 Release 附件 `build-source.json`，不把运行中的工作流写成已通过。

未安装或部署到真机；模拟器和合成订阅测试不证明真实订阅服务、所有网络及长期运行正常。Issue #426 的现场根因仍未证实，保留开放等待脱敏现场复测，不以合并 PR 或发布新版本替代证据。请勿公开订阅 URL、密钥或完整配置。

# MagicNet v1.8.1

本补丁版继续维护现有 Android root / arm64 实现，集中修正订阅处理，并恢复迁移后的正式构建发布入口。

- 多来源订阅聚合保留来自不同来源的同名节点，调整来源身份、节点与代理组引用的处理，减少重名导致的覆盖或聚合失败。
- 统一订阅 URL 的识别和去重：移除不参与请求的片段，保留路径、查询参数和百分号编码的请求含义；前端预览与设备侧保存使用一致规则。
- 调整订阅获取、缓存、配置重建和错误传播，保留节点中的协议字段；修正相关预览、用量显示和自定义分流兼容处理。
- 正式发行继续放在 MagicNet 仓库。构建、质量检查和 Android/KernelSU 模拟器验收使用同一固定源码提交；附件先上传草稿，核对清单及 SHA-256 后再公开。

## 安装与更新

`magicnet_installer.zip`、`MagicNet.zip` 和 `MagicNet-core.zip` 是同一核心包的兼容下载名，模块 ID 均为 MagicNet。`MagicNet-full.zip` 包含离线组件，适合首次安装或网络不便时使用。组件 ZIP 不作为独立模块安装。

更新会保留用户配置和订阅；完成后按管理器提示重启。下载后可用同页的 `SHA256SUMS` 校验完整性，校验和不是独立公钥签名。

默认仍为 `tun` / `magicnet0`，只允许显式选择 `tun|ebpf`。eBPF 可用性取决于设备内核及 cgroup/TC 能力。

## 验证范围与已知限制

正式发行由关联 Actions 的模块、安装迁移、组件、完整质量检查及 Android/KernelSU 模拟器门槛共同放行。模拟器和合成测试不代表 arm64 真机、真实订阅服务、加密服务器互通、多厂商网络或长期运行已经验收。

本版不宣称已确认 Issue #426 的现场根因，也不把工作流通过视为全部多来源订阅场景或独立重建合同均已完成。遇到订阅问题时，请提供脱敏后的来源数量、失败阶段及诊断状态，勿提交订阅 URL 或密钥。

# MagicNet v1.8.0

本版按照当前 Recipkg 配方修正软件，在原有 Rust、Shell、Vue 实现上继续开发。

- 节点与代理组页新增应用、域名和自定义组/出口编辑，草稿先预览，再保存并应用。
- 自定义项通过有归属的增量层生成，保留订阅和系统管理项；订阅更新重新生成时保留自定义项，撤销时保留订阅新增项。发生名称碰撞、组循环或外部冲突时拒绝覆盖。
- 应用选择可读取 Android 主用户的应用名称，支持名称和包名搜索。清单与凭据不进入通用操作输出。
- WebUI 改为矿白、石墨与玉绿配色，保留 14 个页面、原有操作流程、中英俄切换与浅深色主题。
- 包含此前合并的代理组兼容、订阅应用锁、安装与配置恢复修正。

## 安装与更新

Android arm64 root 模块。完整包 `MagicNet-full.zip` 适合离线安装；轻量安装包 `magicnet_installer.zip` 通过已发布的组件清单获取组件。安装前保留自己的配置，更新后按管理器提示重启。下载后可用同一发布页的 `SHA256SUMS` 核对完整性；这不是私钥签名。

默认透明代理仍为 `tun`（`magicnet0`），仅支持显式切换 `tun|ebpf`。eBPF 仍受设备内核能力限制。

## 验证范围

发布前执行本地 Rust、WebUI、浏览器、Android 构建及安装包检查；具体结果记录在配方的验证记录中。浏览器的模拟设备任务和安装夹具不等于真实网络验收。多厂商 Play/GMS、热点双栈、Tailnet 连通性及长期性能场景仍需各自的真实设备证据。

本地验证：Rust 808 passed / 1 ignored，前端 338 项，全套浏览器 747 passed / 3 skipped；字体统一后的布局复查 244 passed / 2 skipped。安装升级、模拟 Magisk 生命周期、9 个组件和最终安装器检查通过。实际 Android 安装与联网尚未验收。

配方归档 `magicnet-0.2.0.recipe.tar.gz` 和完整构建提示词 `magicnet-0.2.0-build.md` 随本版提供。源码固定在本仓库 v1.8.0 标签，main 继续维护配方；重建方法见 [README](https://github.com/LIghtJUNction/MagicNet#重建指南)。

# MagicNet v1.8.7

## 证书策略默认关闭

- 系统证书禁用功能默认关闭，未配置 enabled 时按 false 处理。
- 开机 apply 在未启用或已关闭时直接返回，保持系统证书状态。
- 需要禁用时可显式运行 certificate-policy disable，preview 与 restore 继续可用。
- 保留已经明确设置的用户意图。曾手动禁用的证书需要显式恢复。

本地真实 X.509 回归覆盖默认关闭、开机无操作、显式禁用、恢复、幂等与归属冲突恢复。

## 模拟器验收修复

- 修复 Wi-Fi 上联故障注入后只恢复链路、未恢复 Android Wi-Fi 框架关联的问题。
- 前台和独立延迟恢复 guard 使用相同的系统 Wi-Fi 恢复流程，并有界等待接口重建。
- 保留恢复后真实默认路由、TUN、就绪和同应用 UID TCP 流量验收，报告门禁核对恢复方法。

## 下载哪个？

- **多数人**：`QSC-Battery_v*-full.zip`（双守护 + WebUI，可内嵌伴侣 APP；在线更新也指向它）
- **只要脚本、包要小**：`…-lite.zip`（无 WebUI / 无内嵌 APK / 无守护）
- **其它模块包**：`-rust` / `-c` 只带对应守护；`-sh` 有 WebUI、守护可后装
- **`QSC-Battery_v*.apk`**：伴侣 APP；非 lite 模块刷入时也可选装，不必单独下
- **`qscd-rust-*` / `qscd-c-*`**：事件守护单文件；一般由 full 自带或 WebUI 下载，**不要当模块刷**

完整说明：[安装与升级](https://eikeitsu.github.io/QSC-Battery/guide/install.html)

## 更新说明

- **KernelSU Next 模块横幅**：增加模块背景横幅，使用ksu next管理器开启模块背景横幅可以给模块增加图片背景；
- **KernelSU 模块仓库**：仓库根目录增加 `module.yaml`（便于提交 modules.kernelsu.org），为将模块提交至ksu官方模块仓库做准备
- **音量键 volkey**：`bin/volkey`（`EVIOCGRAB`）供安装 customize 与 Action 共用，避免 BakaSU 等管理器不吞键时弹出系统音量条；SukiSU 管理器常自吞 KeyEvent。缺二进制时回退 `getevent`
- **Lint**：接入 `lint:py`（ruff）、`lint:clang`、`lint:rust`、`lint:kotlin`（缺工具本机跳过 / CI 强制）；`format:all` 与 lint-staged 覆盖 py / C / Rust / Kotlin

### v1.6.0 (10600) - 2026-11-05
`ACC: dev-2025-06-06`

WebUI 🎛️ ->
- Added language switcher to the WebUI banner.
- Added animated gradient glow to the WebUI banner border to indicate active charging.
- Added system information line to the WebUI banner displaying the root solution, Android version, and kernel version.
- Added automatic daemon restart on configuration reset.
- Added dynamic `accd` description system with real-time status and charging thresholds (@LegacyFreeman).
- Added multi-language localization support (de-DE, fr-FR, pt-PT, ru-RU, tr-TR, zh-CN, zh-TW) (@LegacyFreeman). *Only Russian currently has a complete WebUI translation; the other languages currently include shell translations only. WebUI translations can be contributed through [Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/project/acc-with-webui).*
- Centralized WebUI and Shell (action button, module description, and installation) translations in Crowdin as the single source of truth.
- Added documentation language switcher and corrected header layout in `README.md` (@LegacyFreeman).
- Fixed `module.prop` initialization and prevented infinite loops during background state updates (@LegacyFreeman).
- Fixed WebUI components (`App.svelte`, `Toast.svelte`, `DropdownModal.svelte`, `banner.svelte.js`) and build workflow integration (@LegacyFreeman).
- Fixed unwanted long-press highlighting of dropdown items in *WebUI X: Portable (WXP)* while preserving selected item styling.
- Fixed unwanted text selection on the WebUI banner title and subtitle.
- Fixed `Test All` card not autoscrolling correctly upon opening.
- Fixed visual synchronization for `Charging Thresholds`, `Idle Mode`, and `Reset Battery Stats` so they update instantly on configuration reset.
- Updated npm dependencies.

## AEGIS // FIREWALL v1.0.0

First public release.

- Blacklist and whitelist modes, each with its own rule set
- Per-app control for Wi-Fi, mobile data, VPN, LAN and roaming, IPv4 and IPv6
- Host rules: block or allow a domain, IP or CIDR, optionally per port and protocol, per app or for all apps
- Temporary access (15 min, 1 h, 8 h) that reverts on its own
- Screen-off blocking with a configurable delay
- Rules for every Android user: Dual apps, Second space, work profiles
- Rules applied at boot, before the device is unlocked, in one atomic iptables-restore per address family
- Watchdog that restores the OUTPUT hook if the system removes it
- Live connections per app with one-tap address blocking
- Per-app blocked counters on any kernel, plus kernel LOG when available
- Profiles, backup and restore
- Lockdown kill switch in the WebUI and on the module Action button
- Diagnostics: kernel capability probe, hook state, daemon log, restore errors

Requires a kernel with the iptables owner match (all GKI kernels). The installer checks this and aborts if it is missing.

releases.body:
## APEX // APPS v1.0.0

First public release.

- Every preinstalled app is matched against a built-in safety list and labelled Safe, Careful or Required
- Apps the system depends on are refused outright, so a bad tap cannot break the boot
- Disable, hide (keeps all data) or freeze apps, one at a time or in bulk, per Android user
- Snapshots: a snapshot is taken automatically before any batch change, and restoring one only turns apps back on
- Review tab groups preinstalled apps by consequence, with bulk actions per group
- Background permissions per app: run in background, wake lock, start at boot, clipboard, overlays, usage access, installing other apps
- Battery policy per app: standby bucket and the Doze whitelist
- Backups to Download/APEX with the app files and, optionally, its data
- Dual apps and second space are handled as separate users
- A change journal with a one-tap undo of the last change
- Action button prints a summary of everything changed so far

Nothing is changed at install time. Requires a WebUI-capable root manager.
releases.name: v1.0.0

首个公开发行版本。

- 放行 `allow untrusted_app fuse_device chr_file { read write }`，修复 CloudDrive2 挂载网盘报 `IO Permission denied error 13`
- 保持 SELinux 强制模式（Enforcing），不使用 `setenforce 0`，不影响银行类检测 App
- `post-fs-data.sh` 用 `ksud sepolicy apply` 兜底重放规则并记录策略 md5
- `service.sh` 输出 SELinux / 策略 / 挂载状态到 `/data/adb/clouddrive2_fusepatch.log`

releases.body:
📝 English Changelog ### 🆕 New Features - 🩺 Property areas unreadable from the app domain can now be spoofed - 🚀 WebUI now uses KernelSU pm/io interfaces — package enumeration and file I/O without shell forks - 🔄 Template conversion runs fully in the frontend: import legacy module ZIP / system.prop directly, no CLI or temp files - 🎯 Online template library now searches by description and fetches one aggregated file instead of per-file requests - 🧩 Completed custom_props explicit directives and __DELETE__ (soc_model / android_version families, sdk_int deletable) - 🪟 Foreground detection now uses the TOP set, so split-screen / floating windows are no longer misjudged - 🏷️ Log now carries a version banner (version + git hash + build time) ### 🐛 Bug Fixes - 🛡️ Fixed config being unreadable after Zygisk Next 1.5.3's extensive sepolicy.rule changes, which silently disabled all spoofing (config is now read by companion) - 🎲 Fixed random device model when several templates declare the same package (deterministic by config order, with a WebUI warning) - 🇨🇳 Fixed installer text falling back to English on Chinese devices - 🔍 Fixed WebUI clone config resolution; editing a clone no longer wipes the main app entry - 🧹 Fixed duplicate rows and false "configured" badges for one app instance, with explicit config scope labels - 🕵️ Property area copies now use anonymous-mapping camouflage - 🧪 Fixed properties not applying during the cold-start window in hybrid mode (in-process COW now also runs with companion_resetprop) ### ⚡ Improvements - 🏎️ Zero-fork property reads in companion — existence checks and backups query the property areas directly - 👻 Never write properties absent on this ROM — no more enumerable ghost properties - 📦 Module no longer bundles device_faker_cli, shrinking the package - 🧱 cow_props split into 11 modules for clearer responsibilities - ⬆️ Dependency upgrades: rsbinder 0.11, 20+ WebUI dependencies, CI now on NDK r30
### 🆕 新功能 - 🩺 app 域不可读的属性区也能伪装 - 🚀 WebUI 接入 KernelSU pm/io 接口，包枚举与文件读写全程零 shell fork - 🔄 模板转换改纯前端，直接导入旧模块 ZIP / system.prop，无需 CLI 与临时文件 - 🎯 在线模板库支持按模板描述搜索，一次拉取聚合文件替代逐文件请求 - 🧩 补齐 custom_props 显式指令与 __DELETE__（soc_model / android_version 删族、sdk_int 可删除） - 🪟 前台应用检测改用 TOP 集合，多窗口 / 小窗下不再误识别 - 🏷️ 日志新增版本 banner（版本号 + git hash + 构建时间） ### 🐛 修复 - 🛡️ 修复因 Zygisk Next 1.5.3 的 sepolicy.rule 大改导致读不到配置伪装全部失效（配置改由 companion 读取） - 🎲 修复多模板声明同一包名时机型随机（命中改为 config 书写顺序，WebUI 提示争用） - 🇨🇳 修复中文设备安装文案显示英文 - 🔍 修复 WebUI 分身配置解析错位、编辑分身会误删主应用条目 - 🧹 修复同一应用实例重复显示与「已配置」误判，并标注配置作用范围 - 🕵️ 属性区副本改为匿名映射伪装 - 🧪 修复 hybrid 模式冷启动窗口内属性未生效（companion_resetprop 也跑进程内 COW） ### ⚡ 改进 - 🏎️ companion 读取属性零 fork —— 存在性判定与备份直接查属性区 - 👻 属性写入「本机不存在就不写」，不再留下可枚举的幽灵属性 - 📦 模块不再打包 device_faker_cli，安装包体积减小 - 🧱 cow_props 拆分为 11 个模块，职责分层便于维护 - ⬆️ 依赖全量升级：rsbinder 0.11、WebUI 依赖 20+ 项、CI 升 NDK r30

### 🆕 新功能
- 🏷️ Build层新增 Build.BOARD / Build.SOC_MODEL 伪装
- 📅 新增 security_patch 安全补丁日期伪装字段
- 🆔 新增 display_id / incremental 专用伪装字段
- 📐 新增按应用 DPI 伪装支持
- ✏️ WebUI 自定义属性伪装开放编辑
- 📦 安装脚本 Zygisk 检测兼容独特 Zygisk 实现
- 🔗 关注模块弹窗新增官网入口

### 🐛 修复
- 🔄 修复前台门控两类失效 — 应用首启竞态与 packages.list 快照过期
- 🌐 修复在线模板库大量加载失败
- 🧹 修复开关改回默认后键值残留问题
- 🎯 修复多开包名「已配置」状态误判
- 🔒 属性区改用进程私有副本，消除 maps 中的 rw-p 指纹
- ⏱️ 切后台恢复提速至 0.5 秒

### ⚡ 改进
- 🏎️ 长属性值支持原地更新，无需删除重建
- 🤖 rsbinder 升级至 0.10，适配 Android 10~17
- 🗑️ 移除 CPU 伪装功能
- 🔇 非 debug 模式下模块与 companion 完全静默
- 🚀 WebUI 首屏路径瘦身与应用列表性能优化
- 💾 安装脚本默认保留已有配置

releases.body:
# Changelog

## Unreleased

## 0.2.2-Stable - 2026-11-09

### Lite

- Publish a Zygisk-free Lite ZIP with the Tricky Store manager, RKP workbench and
  device RKP issuer. Full remains the default update edition.
- Publish independent SPDX inventories, build-provenance and SBOM attestations
  for both editions in the same release.

### Device Faker

- Add per-app device profiles, reusable templates and installed app selection. Resolve
  profiles and target assignments separately for each Android user.
- Embed 207 searchable device presets contributed by SkyQiQiQwQ in Issue #48.
  Preserve supplied identity, marketing and build fields without filling missing values.
  Review and edit presets before adding them to a draft; saving and enabling remain separate.
- Add brand filtering, fingerprint mismatch notices and accessible field review across
  all 16 locales, including narrow layouts and right-to-left text.

### Play Integrity

- Add Full injection mode and expose process-level activation diagnostics in the WebUI.
- Default the engine to disabled unless explicitly enabled. Keep existing explicit
  enable settings and leave configuration import, preview and application independent
  of the power setting.

### Remote Key Provisioning

- Allow users to include a build fingerprint explicitly in remote signing requests.
- Recognize `rkpdapp.google.apk` in the system RKP APEX for device V1 provisioning.

### Language spoofing

- Add per-app and per-user language rules in the Full edition through Zygisk.

### ZRAM

- Add swap inventory, runtime ZRAM configuration and opt-in boot profiles. Protect
  devices managed by the system and preserve saved settings across failed changes.

### Linux environments

- Reject ARM64 core dumps, malformed load segments and unavailable ELF interpreters
  during import; resolve interpreter paths within the guest filesystem.
- Distinguish zombie processes from live guests and reject symbolic links used as
  private state directories.
- Preserve edited drafts across external configuration changes, identify invalid fields
  and distinguish empty logs from missing environments across all 16 locales.

- Preserve cancellation codes during decompression, handle concurrent cgroup removal,
  and verify the final init identity and supervisor lease before confirming stop.
- Drain final log output, refresh active runtime state without filling operation history,
  and make inspection feedback, cancelled imports and disabled settings explicit.

- Import trusted ARM64 rootfs archives with inspected SHA-256 verification, bounded
  extraction, asynchronous progress, cancellation and private staging.
- Manage private mounts, terminal entry, foreground services, DNS, bounded logs and
  optional startup after boot. Use PID namespaces or cgroup v2 to track guest processes.
- Confirm changes against the current configuration revision and preserve data when
  termination cannot be verified. Keep all 16 locales and RTL layouts aligned with
  existing interface components.

### Kernel modules

- Reject duplicate or unreadable ELF metadata sections, and mark inferred or repeated
  module names explicitly during inspection.
- Validate load parameters by UTF-8 bytes before confirmation, with localized field errors
  and persistent inspection progress/error feedback across 16 locales.
- Protect the `kernelsu` root core from unloading, reject unknown holder state, and
  expose protection reasons consistently in the backend and all 16 interface locales.
- Use explicit confirmation action labels and isolate module names in RTL sentences;
  preserve confirmation content through close transitions and label module taint accurately.
- Add a separate Linux kernel module browser with loaded/sysfs-only state, references,
  dependents, runtime metadata and read-only parameters.
- Browse standard Android module directories and inspect uncompressed `.ko` ELF metadata.
- Add confirmed, serialized runtime load/unload operations with inspected-file digest checks,
  dependency checks, kernel-enforced restrictions and explicit unknown-outcome timeout reports.
- Match Android kernel procfs variants and keep release-prefix comparison advisory for
  symbol-versioned modules. Check ELF class/byte order and preserve parameter whitespace.
- Validate worker protocol/results, bound process cleanup, and retain partial read failures.
- Add localized runtime states, isolated technical strings, persistent operation feedback,
  keyboard focus restoration and layouts that adapt to larger text across 16 locales.

## 0.2.1-Stable - 2026-10-26

### Play Integrity

- Fetch selectable Pixel release fingerprints from Google build metadata, with
  Pixel 6a selected by default. Preview candidates and save their source metadata
  without applying them or enabling the engine. Leave unknown patch dates unset.
- Add quick controls for Build, property and Play Store fingerprint overrides.
  Explain the Play Store SDK compatibility mode and its precedence over fingerprints.
- Preview system, vendor and boot patch policies separately while retaining
  unselected partition settings and backend-specific formats.
- Persist process restart and device reboot requirements across page reloads.
  Keep independent keystore recovery available when an activation marker fails.
- Compare process-local Build and property snapshots with the saved configuration,
  matching revision, boot identity, PID and process start time. Import decoded
  integrity reports as unverified summaries; missing labels remain unknown.
- Extend configuration, recovery, JNI and mobile browser regression coverage,
  including narrow English, Chinese and right-to-left layouts. Local diagnostics
  and tests do not establish a Google Play Integrity verdict.

### Translations

- Add Ukrainian and Polish translations and localize the new integrity controls.

## 0.2.0-Stable - 2026-10-24

### Integrity and keystore compatibility

- Keep OEM lock-state and AVB property changes in their appropriate boot stages,
  including when Play Integrity is disabled, unconfigured or falls back after a failure.
- Validate SHA-256/SHA-512 boot hashes against backend requirements before saving.
  Preserve independent OhMyKeymint trust settings when only the prop handler changes.
- Serialize keystore configuration writes, restore failed updates, retain unknown
  default and per-app policy fields, and reject stale configuration or backend selections.
- Keep unsaved property and policy edits across background refreshes. Add explicit
  property reload and report settings that require a reboot.
- Align module disable/remove handling across the CLI, shell and native companion.
  Reject invalid compatibility options consistently without changing saved enable intent.
- Respect separate system, vendor and boot patch values when preparing optional
  keystore synchronization. Retain explicit configurations and skip incompatible
  single-date updates.

### Device provisioning

- Add MediaTek SoC detection, AIDL V1 RKP support and TrustKernel device-ID
  provisioning while retaining Qualcomm-specific defaults and backend selection.
- Refuse contradictory platform evidence and retain diagnostics for failed native
  provisioning. Firmware support and successful hardware issuance remain device-specific.

### Verification

- Extend configuration rollback, lifecycle, native/JVM, contract and mobile WebUI
  regression coverage, including API 36 AVD checks with KernelSU 3.3.0 and
  OhMyKeymint 1.2.0-b12557c.
- Local tests and emulator behavior do not establish Google Play Integrity verdicts
  or physical-device TEE, fingerprint and display compatibility.

## 0.1.8-stable - 2026-10-24

### Play Integrity

- Integrate a separately built Play Integrity Fork-derived engine with an opt-in
  configuration workflow, generation of Pixel Canary candidates, compatibility
  controls, diagnostics and history. Candidate generation and local configuration
  do not guarantee any Google Play Integrity verdict.
- Preview changes before applying configuration or optional keystore patch policies.
  Support structured field editing, raw import/export, saved profiles, migration,
  rollback, and confirmation before recovering an interrupted update.
- Make engine activation and emergency disable independent from configuration reads,
  including during errors and pending cleanup. Restore managed state when disabling.
- Improve phone-sized layouts: consistent navigation, panels, editor controls and
  preview alignment. Preserve drafts while switching tabs and correct Back behavior.

### Reliability and updates

- Paginate command history and diagnose empty backend responses.
- Handle different fingerprint-generator output paths and improve its diagnostics.
- Fall back to an English release download link when a Telegram ZIP exceeds the
  Bot API's upload limit.

### Licensing and verification

- Keep the derived engine under GPLv3 with upstream notices, and retain the
  independently implemented management interface under MIT.
- Link to the immutable build commit for corresponding source rather than
  embedding a duplicate source archive in the module.
- Add independent engine compilation, packaging checks, contract tests and
  mobile WebUI regression coverage to CI.

## 0.1.7-stable - 2026-10-19

### Tricky Store manager

- Accept EC-only keyboxes for OhMyKeymint while retaining certificate-chain and
  certificate-count validation for every supplied key.
- Preserve legacy and modern Xposed module detection with zip 9 through exact
  central-directory path lookups, including APKs with non-UTF-8 filenames.

### Dependencies

- Upgrade zip to 9.0.4 and refresh Rust and WebUI dependencies and lockfiles.

## 0.1.6-stable - 2026-10-18

### WebUI

- Run shell commands through the host's queued job API when available, so slow
  commands no longer block return navigation. Preserve output, exit status and
  compatibility with hosts that only provide `exec`.
- Stop restarting failed automatic update checks on each return to the home page;
  keep manual retries and channel changes available. Read the fixed hosting module
  identity once per WebUI session.
- Reduce target-list reconstruction overhead with shallow query snapshots, stable
  drafts and lightweight selection indicators. Measure new virtual rows through
  ResizeObserver to avoid repeated forced layout, including with enlarged text.
- Clean up command callbacks on completion and launch failures, including hosts
  that report a companion error after a nonzero exit.

## 0.1.5-stable - 2026-10-18

### WebUI

- Virtualize target and system-app lists while preserving search, bulk selection,
  keyboard focus and per-app controls. Batch synchronous package metadata lookups
  and stop queued lookups when their query is cancelled.
- Preserve edits made during target saves, update the saved baseline without an
  extra package-manager query, and guard overlapping writes.
- Keep RKP navigation available during loading, prevent overlapping profile
  operations, and discard results for changed inputs.
- Fix cached Device ID form initialization, language-switch races, cancelled file
  reads and malformed repository messages. Bound uploads and translation requests.
- Adapt buttons, tabs, forms, menus, dialogs and sheets to narrow screens, landscape
  and enlarged text. Wrap technical values and application names, improve supporting
  text size and contrast, and respect display safe areas.

## 0.1.4-stable - 2026-10-17

### RKP Workbench

- Add **Import DICE materials** as the main workbench entry, with separate offline
  validation, diagnostic CSR construction and online issuance commands. An existing CSR
  is not required; device collection and firmware patching are not implemented here.
- Preserve the imported chain, match explicit signing material to its leaf key, and
  construct a new CSR v3 using a fresh server challenge and newly generated attestation key.
- Share issuance and export between imported material and the labelled experimental
  degenerate-chain mode. Remove implicit offline fallback and successful error results.
- Select returned chains by public key, verify certificate signatures and constraints,
  and publish private keyboxes atomically after XML readback checks. JSON results contain
  paths and summaries instead of private XML. Installation remains independent.
- Bump the workbench feature contract to 2. Old profiles retain their seed derivation;
  material import does not overwrite profiles or an installed keybox.
- Accepts the integer DICE mode allowed by the `android.14` profile.
- Verification uses generated synthetic keys and a local simulated server. Real-material
  production acceptance and successful production export remain unverified for this path.

### Device RKP Issuer
- Automatic mode tries V2, AIDL V1 and native V1 in order, skipping unavailable methods.
  Any issuance or validation failure advances to the next method with a fresh challenge;
  failures are aggregated only after every method fails. Successful results include an
  attempt history. Local file writes happen after certificate validation succeeds.
- Adds the `v1-native` backend for vendor command `0x311e`. Native V1 reuses the
  V1 CSR assembler, structural checks and isolated worker, and does not require a system
  AIDL APK at runtime. Firmware and server acceptance remain unverified.
- Reports protocol and backend separately, exposes native V1 resource availability,
  and uses feature contract 5 across the CLI and WebUI.
- Adds the V1 AIDL signing oracle for Qualcomm PureSoft firmware with a zero HBK,
  adapted from LazyBonesLZY/rkp-v1-oracle under its MIT license.
- Adds automatic and explicit V1/V2 protocol selection.
- Selects the full EEK chain for the HAL's reported curve and uses the device's AIDL
  proxy in an isolated process, with bounded exchange files and timeout cleanup.
- Reports V1 as structurally checked; encrypted signing evidence is verified by the
  provisioning server. V2 retains local signature verification.
- Cross-checks Qualcomm aliases (including QTI/QCOM), SoC part numbers, hardware properties
  and kernel SoC information. Unknown and conflicting evidence have separate blockers;
  empty properties no longer imply support. The WebUI shows the evidence and keeps firmware
  and server compatibility unverified.
- Recognizes QTI as Qualcomm and gives the isolated worker vendor library search paths,
  retaining the default namespace's system dependency links for libraries such as libcrypto.
- Preserves worker error types and accepts bare as well as field-61-wrapped CSRs.
- Bounds exchange-file reads, rejects nonregular files and symlinks, and requires exactly
  one nonempty certificate chain for the requested key.
- Reserves private output directories atomically, removes partial runs on write failure,
  and saves keyboxes and private keys with mode `0600`, including explicit output copies.
- Uses the prerequisite report's device fingerprint consistently; an explicit fingerprint
  can satisfy a missing fingerprint without bypassing other prerequisites.
- Corrects the key export description: the exported keybox includes a software-generated
  private key; this path does not extract a private key from the TEE.

### TEE Attestation Extractor
- New offline tool for extracting Keybox XML and PEM material from existing captures and
  verifying private-key correspondence, certificate signatures and chain completeness.
- Verifies candidate RKP identity material against the signing leaf of a locally verified
  CSR, with separate Ed25519-seed, P-256-seed and P-256-scalar modes and raw capture offsets.
- Returns summaries without exposing private material. Explicit exports use private output
  directories and owner-only files; mismatched identity material cannot be exported.
- Adds binary uploads, device file paths, manager installation through an extension point,
  and translations in all 14 languages. Device-side acquisition is not included.
- Local checks do not establish root trust, revocation status, registration or server acceptance.
  Supported private keys are EC P-256/P-384 and RSA 2048–8192; RSA-1024 is unsupported.
- Verifies private-key PEM labels against their DER encoding. Inline inputs are limited
  to 32 KiB per file to fit shell transport; device file paths accept up to 256 KiB.
- Finds XML document boundaries through parsed tags, accepts closing-tag whitespace,
  and rejects illegal XML characters before exporting material.
- Rejects trailing data in CSR CBOR items, including embedded signed payloads, protected
  headers, DICE subject keys and configuration descriptors.
- Resolves same-name certificate issuers by signature and handles self-issued key rotation
  certificates without treating them as self-signed roots.
- Ignores root-tag examples in XML comments outside the captured document.

### WebUI
- Keeps long error details, links and code within the viewport.

### Command wrapper
- Preserves backend failure exit codes and tries fallback binaries only after execution
  failures (`126` or `127`).

## 0.1.3-stable - 2026-10-17

### Device RKP Issuer
- New tool: signs a P-256 key we generated with this device's Qualcomm KeyMint TA
  (`CSR_V2`, command `0x3122` over `libkeymasterdeviceutils.so`) and submits the resulting
  `AuthenticatedRequest` to Google's RKP server, then exports `keybox.xml` plus its private
  key. The request does not extract a private key from the TEE.
- Warns twice before it can run, and the backend refuses a run without
  `--acknowledge-limitations`: only some devices work, and only RKP certificates can be
  issued.
- Checks Android arm64, root, `/dev/smcinvoke`, `libkeymasterdeviceutils.so` and a Qualcomm
  SoC first, and reports exactly which prerequisite is missing.
- Validates the device's CSR (DICE chain, signature, challenge, `keysToSign`) and binds the
  issued certificate chain to the generated key before writing anything. The chain must also
  be one leaf-to-root path with no certificate left off it. These local shape and key
  checks do not establish certificate trust, revocation status or server acceptance.

## 0.1.2-stable - 2026-10-11

### Tricky Store manager
- Complete port of Tricky Addon (Update Target List):
  - Target list with modes, per-app policy, search, bulk selection, DenyList, unnecessary
    apps, system apps and auto-add.
  - Keyboxes from AOSP, "unknown", a local file, the keybox repository and custom providers,
    with import and export.
  - Prop settings, default policy with *Today*, help, keyboard shortcuts and its 23
    translations, including right-to-left languages.
- One manager for Tricky Store (`config.ini` and legacy `target.txt`), TEESimulator
  (`config.json`) and OhMyKeymint (`config.toml` + `injector.toml`).
  - The validation rules follow each module's own sources.
  - Unknown sections, comments and keys are preserved.
- Optional WebUI entry on the keystore module (plus the action button on Magisk), and the
  TSupport-Advance auto-target stop flag.
- Tricky Addon's in-app translation update, translation guide and Telegram link.
- Checked against the real modules on a KernelSU device, which found and fixed:
  - OhMyKeymint v1.2.0 rejected our `injector.toml` (an unknown `version` key) while the
    WebUI reported success. `[scoop.<package>]` tables are now read and written like
    OhMyKeymint's own parser does.
  - The "unknown" keybox now gives each key a two-certificate chain. Tricky Addon's
    single-certificate keybox only loads on Tricky Store: TEESimulator and OhMyKeymint
    refuse it.
  - TEESimulator accepts EC-only keyboxes, such as the RKP workbench exports.
  - Saving tells when OhMyKeymint needs a restart to apply a change.

### WebUI
- Rebuilt on Vue 3.5, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn-vue.
  - A black and white theme, light or dark, where color only marks errors, success and
    warnings.
  - Designed for phones along Material 3 Expressive:
    - 48dp touch targets and a visible response to every press.
    - Round buttons that square up while pressed, segmented lists, and spring motion.
    - A large title that collapses into the 64dp app bar, for one-handed reach.
    - Tonal gray surfaces instead of borders and shadows, with contrast checked
      against WCAG.
  - Menus, tabs and button groups mirror in right-to-left languages too.
  - Follows the KernelSU manager's window insets.
  - The Android back gesture closes dialogs and sheets.
- Every tool in 14 languages: English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean,
  Spanish, French, German, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, Vietnamese and
  Indonesian.
- Help: long links and code wrap inside the page, and two slips in upstream translations
  (a link missing its parenthesis, a code span closed with a quote) no longer show raw
  Markdown.
- Every tool is a self-contained feature folder, discovered automatically.
  - Features plug into each other only through extension points.
  - Every backend response is validated against a schema.
- A tool whose backend feature is missing or on another contract version is disabled
  instead of misreading data.
- Unit tests (Vitest) and end-to-end tests (Playwright against a mock KernelSU host) with
  light, dark, right-to-left and Chinese screenshots.
- Contract tests run every API call through `duckctl.sh` and a real `duckd` build and
  parse the results with the WebUI's schemas.
- Device tests (`scripts/device-test.sh`) drive the WebUI inside the real KernelSU manager
  with each keystore module installed.
- Loads as seven files instead of about eighty. The KernelSU manager reads each request
  through a root shell, so this halved the load time on a slow device.
- Type-checked on the TypeScript 7 engine through typescript-native-bridge.

### Backend
- `duckd` builds its CLI from a feature registry. `duckd features` reports the compiled-in
  features, and each feature can be built alone.
- New `system` feature: module and device summary, stable and canary updates with changelog,
  output files, command history, uninstall and reboot.
- RKP profiles read their device defaults from AOSP build properties.
- Updated RustCrypto to its current generation (p256/p384 0.14, ed25519/x25519 3, aes-gcm
  0.11, x509-cert 0.3). Keys derived from saved seeds are pinned by regression tests.

### Module
- Scripts follow the KernelSU module guide:
  - Late-load support (`late-load.sh`).
  - A late prop pass after boot for values the system sets late.
  - The module description goes into KernelSU's temporary config.
- Magisk runs the boot-completed work from `service.sh`.
- The prop handler adds `ro.boot.vbmeta.size`, and applies the boot hash even when the
  handler is disabled, as upstream does.
- Uninstalling removes entry links, flags and saved data.

### Tooling
- CI fails when any source file in any language exceeds 600 lines.
- CI: NDK r30, Node 24, pnpm 12, WebUI lint/format/unit/E2E, per-feature builds.
- Canary artifacts are the installable module directory.
- Dependabot opens one pull request per major update.
